step-1.text: Stand one side panel on its edge, holes facing in. Screw in four cam pins by hand, then tap in four dowels.

count-1.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 4 cam pins and 4 wood dowels.

step-2.text: Push the bottom panel onto the low pins and dowels. Drop two cam locks into the round holes, arrows facing the pins, and turn them clockwise until they grab.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 bottom panel and 2 cam locks.

step-3.text: The fixed shelf holds the frame square, so it goes in now. Slide onto the pins and lock with cam locks, clockwise.

count-3.text: This step uses 1 fixed shelf and 2 cam locks.

step-4.text: Pins and dowels go into the ends of the panels on this side too. Lower the second side onto all of them at once, then lock the last four cam locks.

count-4.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 4 cam pins, 4 wood dowels and 4 cam locks.

step-5.text: Tap four dowels into the top edges of the sides. Set the top panel on, good side up, then lock it from inside with four cam locks.

count-5.text: This step uses 1 top panel, 4 wood dowels and 4 cam locks.

step-6.text: Tap four dowels into the ends of the plinth board and press it in under the bottom panel, at the front.

count-6.text: This step uses 1 plinth and 4 wood dowels.

step-7.text: Tip the frame onto its front, on a rug or the flattened box so nothing gets scratched.

count-7.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-8.text: Lay the back panel on, smooth side facing in. Line it up with one corner and nail it along the edges, about every twenty centimeters. If the corners line up, the frame is square.

step-9.text: Stand it back up on its feet. Nice, the box is done.

count-9.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-10.text: Screw the metal runners inside the frame, one pair for each drawer, four in all. Use the pre-drilled holes so every pair sits level.

count-10.text: This step uses 4 drawer runners and 8 screws.

step-11.text: First drawer. Lay the drawer front face down on something soft. Tap in four dowels, then press both drawer sides onto them, grooves facing in.

count-11.text: This step uses 1 drawer front, 2 drawer sides and 4 wood dowels.

step-12.text: Slide the thin drawer bottom into the grooves, shiny side up, all the way to the front.

step-13.text: Close the drawer with its back panel, then drive four screws through the back into the sides. Snug, not cranked.

count-13.text: This step uses 1 drawer back and 4 screws.

step-14.text: Now the second drawer, exactly the same way: front, sides, bottom, back. Then slide every drawer in onto its runners until it stops. The demo leaves drawer one pulled open so you can see inside. Take a break halfway if you need one.

count-14.text: This step uses 1 drawer front, 2 drawer sides, 1 drawer bottom, 1 drawer back, 4 wood dowels and 4 screws.

done.text: Done. Your CLYDE 2-drawer nightstand is built. Give it a proud little pat.
